name: intraday-equities-jpm-h20-ridge
notes: JPM H in {5,10,15,20}, ridge baseline. Two changes from run-jpm-h20.json (A0037), both from findings it produced. (1) 2h and 3h flip to cross_session, and 60m does too in the universe variant: an intra-session scale of width W emits NaN for the first W of every 390 RTH minutes and _frame_matrix drops the row, so 3h alone cost 46% of every session permanently. Measured recovery 49.4% -> 77.6% of grid rows. The windows now bridge the overnight gap, which changes what they mean; at this horizon they are regime context, not a directional claim. (2) Ridge with one alpha replaces LightGBM with 32 draws. The tree run showed train IC 0.10-0.31 against val IC ~0 in every fold and an inner-holdout score uncorrelated with fold validation. Still DIAGNOSTIC, not a lock. The vol-normalised label is NOT here - it needs a node change and an ADR.

features.notes: lookback=20 emits one-minute ret_lag columns for the last 20 minutes. Every horizon here is cross_session so none costs rows beyond a one-time warmup; see docs/research/row-loss-is-intra-session-scale-warmup-not-cross-session.md.

tradable.notes: SPY has already entered the residual features; score tradables.

jpm.notes: One name. Sits after tradable so the cohort that built the cross-sectional features is untouched. JPM is split-free across the sample, which is why it is the one kept.

scan.notes: Ridge; the only knob is alpha, swept over six decades on the inner train holdout. Fold validation stays unread. Ridge is scale-sensitive and these columns are not standardised, so alpha ranges high on purpose. hpo_objective stays ic: at this SNR an MSPE search picks the flattest model and a constant forecast is the MSPE optimum outright.

walkforward.notes: Same post-COVID folds as run-hstar-cv-postcovid.json so the two are comparable: first validation 2022-05-06, twenty 63-day steps, a real 730-day bounded training window, last validation inside the 2025-11-30 cut. objective is val_ic, NOT go_frac: counting fold-level rejections and taking the max is vote counting, which Hedges-Olkin showed is inconsistent when per-fold power is below one half (A0035). The winner here only labels a fold in the summary; the science is the per-fold sequence, which is what the block-by-block reading needs. embargo_days=5 is now larger than any label window on this grid (20 minutes), so no training row's label can reach into validation.
